observations.trace: Selected spawn admission maps enemy fixture behavior or startup combat configuration into a package Vec; BotPlugin materializes Added packages into controller/guard/reaction/recovery components. Standard package copies defense dodge chance from config; selected production no later package mutation is established.
observations.remaining: A public retained collection, initial-only materializer and possible debug snapshot are distinct authority questions. Mutation support and all component/config owners remain open.

observations.trace: Debug dump allowlists both the behavior-package component and offensive controller; debug CLI loads a WorldDeserializer DynamicWorld, writes it to newly mapped entities, and flushes. Pinned lock-bound Bevy source describes Added and replacement semantics for queued EntityCommands::insert.
observations.remaining: Conditional on successful snapshot, preserved nondefault phase, subsequent matching Update and deferred insert. No debug endpoint, serializer, loader, scheduler, world or product ran.

observations.trace: resolve_scene_fixture returns Ok(PathBuf) unconditionally, while startup default immediately expects it; the same wrapper is a native Clap value parser, whose pinned function interface requires Result. Native enemy fixture CLI delegates to load and parse; parse validates roster after serde deserialization, but the public derived Deserialize itself exposes a separate constructor without calling validate. The enemy count production expect is bounded by MAX_MOB_COUNT30 only on validated routes.
observations.remaining: The path-rule issue, fixture admission issue and count-rule issue have distinct first contracts. No false normal panic, direct-deserialization execution or actual invalid fixture is asserted.

conditional_findings.first_contract: A restored snapshot that includes a live offensive controller and its declarative behavior must have one explicit authority for the restored controller state.
conditional_findings.source_witness: The debug dump allowlist includes both CombatantBehaviorPackages and OffensiveCombatAi. The debug loader deserializes a DynamicWorld and writes it to fresh mapped entities. The project installs BotPlugin and its Update chain queries newly added CombatantBehaviorPackages; for each OffensiveCombat entry it queues insert(OffensiveCombatAi::default()). The pinned Bevy source describes newly added filters and replacement semantics for insert. OffensiveCombatAi::default has target None and Pursuing phase.
conditional_findings.counterevidence: This is conditional on a successful dump and load containing both components, a nondefault restored controller, the new package being observed by the selected Added query, and the deferred insert being applied afterward. Reflection/serialization success, scheduler timing, a real restored snapshot and intended debug-replay semantics are not observed. The dump is explicitly debug-only, and no strategic or player database is involved.
conditional_findings.effect_and_limits: Under those conditions, the queued default replaces the restored target/phase after restoration. Other independently restored fields and gameplay outcomes are not established.
conditional_findings.repair_direction: When authorized, decide whether the package is a one-time recipe or the restored controller is authoritative; preserve the chosen debug lifecycle without unconditional stale/default overwrites or compatibility shims.
conditional_findings.alias_qualification: A bounded exact-term search of recovered059 ledger and queue found no materialize_behavior_packages or OffensiveCombatAi dump record; global alias status and historical unique count remain open. No checkpoint3821 promotion.

conditional_findings.first_contract: The retained public behavior-package collection and its installed capability components need an explicit lifecycle authority if packages can change after their initial materialization.
conditional_findings.source_witness: CombatantBehaviorPackages publicly holds a Vec of declarative variants. materialize_behavior_packages only selects Added<CombatantBehaviorPackages> and inserts selected capability components, with no removal logic in that function. Pinned Bevy Added documentation describes first-time addition rather than subsequent value changes.
conditional_findings.counterevidence: The selected ordinary spawn creates packages once from validated fixture or config and does not demonstrate any later mutation. One-shot recipe semantics may be intentional; a bounded textual search for Changed/RemovedComponents and direct typed removal is not proof that no other application path exists. No reflection edit or bot ran.
conditional_findings.effect_and_limits: If a retained already-materialized package Vec is changed in place from standard combat to passive after the Added observation, this function does not reprocess it, so its earlier installed offensive and defense components remain unless another owner changes them. Re-adding a package is a separate lifecycle case.
conditional_findings.repair_direction: When authorized, either make one-shot recipe semantics explicit and remove redundant retained authority as appropriate, or reconcile changes and removals through a single owner while preserving intentional package combinations.
conditional_findings.alias_qualification: Related to snapshot initialization but a distinct first contract for post-materialization mutation, not an exact alias by common component remedy. Global aliases and support policy remain open.

conditional_findings.first_contract: The default-scene path must avoid a production expect while preserving the distinct native Clap value-parser contract.
conditional_findings.source_witness: resolve_scene_fixture returns Result<PathBuf,String> but its expression is Ok(resolve_fixture_path(...)); default_scene_input_path immediately expects that result outside tests. The same helper is the Clap value parser for --scene-input. Pinned Clap accepts a fallible Fn(&str) -> Result<T,E> as TypedValueParser and also provides a map adapter for an infallible transformation. The core resolver returns a PathBuf and preserves explicit paths or selects a relative/manifest-based fixture location.
conditional_findings.counterevidence: The selected wrapper constructs Ok on every returning branch, so its expect cannot fail from this wrapper. Its fallible return is a valid native Clap parser boundary; it cannot be discarded without satisfying that API. No CLI parser, path lookup, read failure, panic or startup executed. Enemy fixture parsing/loading errors are a separate fallible contract.
conditional_findings.effect_and_limits: A source-level rule and ownership violation, not an observed panic or evidence that a missing scene is accepted. Actual scene loading can still return its own errors.
conditional_findings.repair_direction: When authorized, remove the outside-test expect by using the infallible resolver in internal default selection, while satisfying Clap’s typed value-parser interface at the actual CLI boundary and preserving explicit and stem path semantics. Do not assume a plain PathBuf-returning function implements the existing fallible parser API.
conditional_findings.alias_qualification: The original059 question specifically did not infer a finding merely from String. The connected production caller establishes the separate outside-test expect rule; this is no global alias or historical unique-count claim.

conditional_findings.first_contract: A value that represents an admitted tactical enemy fixture should enforce its roster and version contract on every supported construction or deserialization path.
conditional_findings.source_witness: TacticalEnemyFixture derives public Deserialize with private fields. Its parse method deserializes and then validates version, nonempty bounded roster, names and loadout; direct deserialization through that derived implementation is a separate public construction path that does not call validate. An otherwise structurally valid fixture with version1 and an empty enemies sequence is rejected by parse validation but has no source-level post-deserialization validator in the derive.
conditional_findings.counterevidence: The selected CLI parser calls load then parse and therefore performs validation, and no malformed fixture, deserializer or command was run. Public fields, type consumers, and whether direct Deserialize is intended as an unvalidated wire DTO remain open.
conditional_findings.effect_and_limits: A conditional admission/ownership gap: a compatible direct deserializer can construct a semantically unvalidated value without using parse. The empty case does not cause the count conversion to overflow and does not prove a runtime failure.
conditional_findings.repair_direction: When authorized, establish one authoritative validated fixture admission or a clearly separate wire representation, preserving real native parsing errors and the explicit CLI validation.
conditional_findings.alias_qualification: No exact TacticalEnemyFixture term was found in a bounded recovered059 queue/ledger search. No global alias absence, historical unique-count change or checkpoint3821 inference.

conditional_findings.first_contract: A production count conversion must follow the repository no-unwrap/expect rule and its actual input invariant.
conditional_findings.source_witness: TacticalEnemyFixture::enemy_count converts enemies.len() to u32 with expect outside tests. The selected parse/CLI path validates a nonempty count at most MAX_MOB_COUNT=30 before use, but derived direct Deserialize is a separate path whose validation remains a distinct admission issue.
conditional_findings.counterevidence: On the selected validated path, 30 fits in u32 and the expect cannot fail for cardinality. An empty directly deserialized fixture also fits; a >u32 roster or real failure is not claimed. This is source-level rule review, not a product test.
conditional_findings.effect_and_limits: Production expect violates the governing Rust rule. Reachable conversion failure, resource feasibility, consumers and exact replacement policy remain open.
conditional_findings.repair_direction: When authorized, remove the outside-test expect using the established fixture admission and explicit conversion contract; do not invent a bogus fallback for validated counts.
conditional_findings.alias_qualification: The production expect is a distinct operation from unvalidated deserialization and fake scene-path Result; share evidence as dependencies but do not infer exact aliases or historical counts.
